Task Spec:
WR-001 — WHATSREPLY: FIX COMPOSE/REVISE SEMANTICS + AUTHOR PROFILE + MESSAGE AUDIO UI

Goal:
Stabilize the AI interaction model before adding case/context infrastructure.

Owner-approved changes:

A) Persistent author profile
- User is male.
- In Russian first-person singular, use masculine grammatical forms when gender is expressed: получил, понял, посмотрел, готов, etc.
- If speaking explicitly on behalf of Lighthouse as “мы”, use plural forms.
- Do not force gender where Russian wording is neutral.

B) Separate AI modes
1. COMPOSE = user says what should be communicated to the recipient.
2. REVISE = user gives an editing instruction about the current draft.
These modes must use different payloads/prompts.

COMPOSE context:
- incoming WhatsApp message
- relevant current contact/thread context
- user instruction describing what to answer
- author profile

REVISE context:
- original incoming message
- CURRENT BEST DRAFT only
- LATEST EDIT INSTRUCTION only
- author profile / relevant context
Do NOT include old failed drafts or prior edit instructions as ordinary conversation history.

C) REVISE system rule
- Edit instruction is a command to the editor, not content for the recipient.
- Never copy meta-comments about editing, gender, tone, model behavior, etc. into the outbound message unless the user explicitly asks to tell the recipient that information.
- Default to minimal/local edits.
- Do not add new meanings, explanations, apologies, justifications or “if you want, I can explain” unless requested.

D) Final self-check before displaying any draft
Verify:
- no user meta-editing comments leaked into recipient text;
- person/gender is correct for the author profile;
- recipient text does not discuss the internal drafting/editing process;
- no unrequested new meaning was introduced.

E) UI
- Make incoming-message and draft/answer containers visually equal in height/weight where practical.
- Add a dedicated “Прослушать входящее” / listen-to-incoming action.
- Keep current Text button for now.
- Preserve one-hand usability and existing voice-first flow.

F) Preserve transport
Do not regress the confirmed path:
WhatsApp Business notification -> WhatsReply -> RemoteInput Reply -> correct WhatsApp chat.

Out of scope for WR-001:
- Outliner/Airtable case linking
- backend/cloud history
- Coexistence/API
- desktop
- case memory architecture
Those are the next phase after this interaction model is verified.
Reasoning Decision: Owner approved this interaction-model fix before adding case/context infrastructure. Root issue: the model currently mixes user editing instructions with recipient-facing content.
Constraints: Do not create a new product layer. Do not touch case linking/backend/Outliner yet. Preserve current working notification/RemoteInput transport and voice-first UX.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Russian first-person drafts use male forms for the owner unless message is explicitly from “мы/Lighthouse”.
2. Saying “Я мужчина, исправь род” in REVISE changes “получила” -> “получил” and does NOT put the explanation about gender into the recipient message.
3. “Сделай мягче/короче/теплее” performs a minimal edit of the current draft, without unrelated new content.
4. Old rejected drafts/edit instructions do not contaminate the next revision.
5. Final self-check blocks obvious meta-editing leakage.
6. Incoming and draft blocks have matched visual treatment/size; incoming message can be listened to separately.
7. Current notification capture and RemoteInput send path still works on the owner’s phone.
8. Build/tests pass; exact tested build/commit and APK artifact are recorded.
9. Builder does not self-approve; hand off for independent verification/user check.
Codex Handoff: Implement WR-001 in the existing WhatsReply repository/app. Preserve the already-working transport. Focus only on prompt/payload separation, persistent author profile, final self-check, and the two UI changes. Build an installable APK and record tested commit/artifact.
